title: Derived sections of one root-tower term with profinite parameters
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a norm-topological finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ containing $E$ with the extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ for every profinite set $P$, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], ordinary unbounded derived categories and total derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $V\to Y$ be an affine etale chart on which the only boundary components present are $V(t_1),\ldots,V(t_r)$, for a reduced strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]; set $Z=V(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ and $V^\circ=V[1/(t_1\cdots t_r)]$. For $r=0$ take $Z=V^\circ=V$. For an affine pro-etale $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to V$, put $S=U\times_V Z$ and
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_1^{1/n},\ldots,x_r^{1/n}]/((x_i^{1/n})^n-t_i)_{i=1}^r\right),\qquad T^\circ=T\times_VV^\circ.$$
The index is ordered by divisibility and the transition sends $x_i^{1/n}$ to $(x_i^{1/m})^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$. Write $j:T^\circ\hookrightarrow T$, $v:T^\circ\to U$, and $s:S\hookrightarrow U$. Setting every root to zero gives $i:S\to T$. When $r=0$ the tower is $T=T^\circ=U$ and $i=s=\mathrm{id}_U$.
For $F=E$ or $\Omega$ let $\mathcal N$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{F,T}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], and fix $i^*\mathcal N\cong p_S^*M_F$, where $M$ is a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space, $M_F(P)=C(P,F\otimes_E M)$, and $F\otimes_E M$ has its finite-dimensional product norm topology. For every profinite set $P$ form $T^\circ[P]$ as in [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], let $v_P:T^\circ[P]\to U$ be the composite, and pull $j^*\mathcal N$ to $T^\circ[P]$. Let $C_F[P]$ be the free internal $C_F$-module on the condensed set $Q\mapsto C(Q,P)$, and write $R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}$ for the right derived internal module Hom. Then restriction of sections and derived adjunction give a natural isomorphism
$$s^*R(v_P)_*(\mathcal N|_{T^\circ[P]}[0])\ \cong\ p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F).$$
It is natural in $P$, in morphisms of the supplied extensions $\mathcal N$, and under pro-etale base change of $U$. It respects automorphisms of the root tower, including continuous profinite families of such automorphisms together with their equivariant actions on $\mathcal N$. For a family indexed by $Q$, the compatibility is the equality of morphisms on the $Q$-parametrized terms, not merely equality after evaluation at each point of $Q$. On degree zero its map is restriction to $S$ of the sections on the full root tower; for $P=*$ it is the inverse of the map induced by $\mathcal N\to Rj_*j^*\mathcal N$. The comparison maps are compatible for $E\to\Omega$ whenever the supplied extensions and boundary identifications are obtained from one $E$-extension by ordinary scalar extension. This compatibility is after scalar restriction and uses the actual map $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Only one term of the root-cover nerve is being computed; no derived invariants or total nerve is identified here. Free internal module means the left adjoint to forgetting a module to a condensed set. Internal module Hom is the right adjoint of internal module tensor; its right derived functor is computed by injective resolutions in its second variable. These are taken in coefficient universes containing the small site and the profinite parameter sets.

proof.text:
Write $q:T\to U$ for the full root morphism, $\pi_P:T[P]\to T$, and $q_P=q\pi_P$. The full parameter extension is $\mathcal N_P=\pi_P^*\mathcal N$. It is lisse, since pullback of a finite free trivialization remains finite free. The root equations commute with base change from $U$ to the affine pro-etale test object $U[P]$; thus $T[P]$ is the same full root construction over $U[P]$. For $J_d=\{1,\ldots,d\}$ put $e_d:T[P]_{J_d}\hookrightarrow T[P]_{J_{d-1}}$. Apply [lem-sfb-root-coordinate-supported-vanishing] to $\mathcal N_P$, with $J=J_{d-1}$ and $a=d$. The support term in the distinguished triangle of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction] is zero, so its second arrow, the actual unit, is an isomorphism $\mathcal N_P|_{T[P]_{J_{d-1}}}[0]\to R(e_d)_*(\mathcal N_P|_{T[P]_{J_d}}[0])$. Start with $d=1$ and compose these isomorphisms for $d=1,\ldots,r$. The normalized derived composition of [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] identifies the composite with the actual unit $\eta_P:\mathcal N_P[0]\to R(j_P)_*j_P^*\mathcal N_P[0]$, where $j_P:T^\circ[P]\hookrightarrow T[P]$. For $r=0$, the composite and unit are identities. Applying $s^*Rq_{P,*}$ and derived composition gives an isomorphism
$$\lambda_P:s^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}s^*R(v_P)_*j_P^*\mathcal N_P[0].$$

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: remove the branches one at a time using their vanishing support terms

proof.text: The morphism $q_P$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: by [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] every finite root algebra is generated by elements satisfying the displayed monic equations and is finite free with basis the monomials of exponents less than $n$; adjoining finitely many such elements gives a finite module by successive division by their monic equations. [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes every such finite stage integral. Every element in the filtered root algebra lies at one finite stage and is therefore integral. Each finite test projection is a finite product of copies of its base ring, also integral; every element of its filtered colimit again lies in a finite stage. These observations apply after base change and prove integrality for their composite $q_P$. Put $B_P=T[P]\times_U S$, with projections $h_P:B_P\to T[P]$ and $q_{S,P}:B_P\to S$. There is a closed immersion $a_P:S[P]\hookrightarrow B_P$ setting all roots to zero. It is surjective on underlying spectra: in the fibre every $x_{a,n}$ is nilpotent since $x_{a,n}^n=0$, so every prime contains every root. Conversely quotienting by all these roots is precisely the ring of $S[P]$. The kernel consists of nilpotents: each element involves finitely many nilpotent roots and an ideal generated by finitely many nilpotents is nilpotent. A common nilpotence exponent for the whole infinite kernel is neither claimed nor needed. The parameter projection satisfies $q_{S,P}a_P=\rho_P:S[P]\to S$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: the integral root algebra and its nilpotent closed fibre

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-closed-base-change] with $q=q_P$, the closed immersion $s:S\hookrightarrow U$, and the lisse module $\mathcal N_P$. The hypotheses established in steps 1 and 2 give the specified exchange isomorphism
$$s^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R(q_{S,P})_*h_P^*\mathcal N_P[0].$$
By [new-lem-weil-pbc-condensed-surjective-closed-equivalence], $a_P^*$ is an equivalence for the actual pulled-back ring $C_F$; hence its actual unit is an isomorphism, not just a comparison of geometric stalks. Its inverse image is exact; the inverse equivalence $a_{P,*}$ is therefore exact too, and its derived functor is its degreewise application. Thus $h_P^*\mathcal N_P[0]\to R(a_P)_*a_P^*h_P^*\mathcal N_P[0]$ is an isomorphism. Derived composition [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] and $q_{S,P}a_P=\rho_P$ identify the last direct image with $R(\rho_P)_*(\rho_P^*i^*\mathcal N[0])$. This uses the nilpotent-fibre equivalence; it does not assert $B_P=S[P]$ as schemes.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: closed exchange and the actual topological-invariance unit

proof.text:
Pull the supplied identification $i^*\mathcal N\cong p_S^*M_F$ back along $\rho_P$. Pullbacks of coefficients compose canonically by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], so $\rho_P^*i^*\mathcal N\cong p_{S[P]}^*M_F$. Now apply [lem-sfb-profinite-constant-derived-functions] with $X=S$ (affine since $S$ is closed in the affine $U$) and the given $M$. Together with step 3 this defines an isomorphism
$$\gamma_P:s^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F).$$
The required map is $\alpha_P=\gamma_P\lambda_P^{-1}$. This produces an isomorphism in the derived module category itself, rather than a family of per-degree identifications.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: identify the constant boundary model and its derived parameter functions

proof.text: All arrows in $\gamma_P$ are the exchange adjunct, the topological-invariance unit, pullback of the supplied boundary identification, and the normalized exponential-law map. Hence in degree zero $\gamma_P$ restricts full-tower sections to $S[P]$ and then regards them as functions of $P$. The arrow $\lambda_P$ is induced by $\mathcal N_P\to R(j_P)_*j_P^*\mathcal N_P$. For $P=*$ the function comparison is the identity, and $\gamma_*$ is the canonical identification with $i^*\mathcal N$: its inverse is induced by the full-tower pullback adjunction and is checked by the triangle identities. Consequently $\alpha_*$ is the inverse of the map induced by that open unit, under this identification. Naturality of units, the normalized composition comparison [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization], and the naturalities explicitly in [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-closed-base-change] and [lem-sfb-profinite-constant-derived-functions] make $\alpha_P$ natural in parameter maps, maps of supplied extensions, and pro-etale base change. For a continuous family of root automorphisms indexed by $Q$, apply the same diagrams after base change $U[Q]\to U$; their action on $\mathcal N$ supplies the module arrow over that base. The parameter naturality of the function comparison gives equality on these $Q$-parametrized diagrams. Inverting $\lambda$ preserves the equality, so this is the required family-level equivariance. Finally the two input comparisons commute after scalar restriction with $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, while the units and restriction of sections commute with that same map. The two commuting squares for $\lambda_E,\lambda_\Omega$ and $\gamma_E,\gamma_\Omega$ imply the square for $\gamma\lambda^{-1}$ by cancellation. No scalar-extension/direct-image isomorphism is inferred.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: normalization, family-level equivariance and actual coefficient map

proof.text: For $r=0$, $T=T^\circ=U$, $S=U$, $\lambda_P$ is the identity, and the construction is exactly the parameter-functions comparison. For $P=\varnothing$, the source is the direct image from the empty scheme and the target is derived Hom from the zero free module, so both are zero. Rank zero and the empty stratum give zero on both sides. For finite $P$, the parameter formula gives the finite product of the $P=*$ models; no passage from finite sets to profinite sets by an unjustified cohomology/limit interchange has been used.
